purpose: One row per Mathlib construction whose axeyum counterpart diverges, so a mirror over it can never honestly flip. Consumed by scripts/check-dispatchable-frontier.py, both to classify the standing open ml430 rows and to SCREEN candidate propositions BEFORE they are preregistered into the nursery. A generator that emits more mirrors over a construction listed here adds unclosable population and inflates the open count without adding work.

constructions.why: Mathlib's `Nat.testBit : Nat -> Nat -> Bool`; this kernel's returns `Nat` in {0,1}. Closing a Bool-typed pinned statement with a Nat-valued proof manufactures a flip. The honest outcome is a local analogue fact (F:nat-testbit-xor, F:nat-lt-of-testbit, F:nat-exists-most-significant-bit, F:nat-zero-of-testbit-eq-zero).

mathlib_source.note: codomain is re-derived by this gate from the pinned statements themselves (a `testBit ... = true/false` occurrence), not taken on trust from this row

constructions.why: Mathlib's `multichoose` is a three-case double recursion (`multichoose n (k+1) + multichoose (n+1) k`) and `multichoose_eq : multichoose n k = (n + k - 1).choose k` is a proved THEOREM about it. Ours DEFINES that closed form as the body. We define what Mathlib proves, about a different function, so the mirrors are different propositions. Showing the two agree needs an induction relating two independently-built Nat.rec instances.

mathlib_source.note: read at the pinned commit; the divergence is in the DEFINITION and is not visible in the pinned statement, so this gate cannot re-derive it -- it is recorded, with the reading, at `recorded_in`

constructions.why: Ours is a fuel-structural linear search; Mathlib's is well-founded on `sqrt n` skipping evens. Same values, different construction, so the pinned statement is about a different function. The local analogue F:nat-coprime-of-lt-minfac is proved.

mathlib_source.note: definitional/algorithmic divergence is invisible in the pinned statement; not re-derivable by this gate

constructions.why: Mathlib's `binaryRec` is `WellFounded.fix` with a DEPENDENT motive. A fuel encoding's non-dependence is forced -- the exhaustion row must return a value for arbitrary `n` with only `motive 0` in hand -- so no amount of infrastructure reaches it. The keystone (F:nat-binary-rec-succ, F:nat-binary-rec-fuel-irrelevance) was built anyway and the mirror still cannot flip.

mathlib_source.note: the divergence is in the recursion principle, not the statement; not re-derivable by this gate

constructions.why: Mathlib's `Squarefree [Monoid R] (r : R) : Prop := ∀ x, x * x ∣ r → IsUnit x` is Prop-valued and lives at the bare root namespace. This kernel declares only the executable decision procedure `Squarefree (n : Nat) : Bool` (nat_prelude/squarefree.rs) -- a Prop-valued predicate admits no evaluation test, so no bridge theorem is built (ADR-0653: an unblocking lane declares the construction and its evaluation test, nothing else). Closing a Prop-typed pinned statement with a Bool-valued proof manufactures a flip.

mathlib_source.note: codomain is re-derived by this gate from the pinned statements themselves (a `Squarefree <arg> →` implication-antecedent occurrence, the mirror image of testBit's `= true/false`), not taken on trust from this row

constructions.why: Mathlib's `noncomputable def nth (p : ℕ → Prop) (n : ℕ) : ℕ` case-splits on `Set.Finite (setOf p)` via `Classical.propDecidable` and, in the infinite branch, appeals to `Nat.Subtype.orderIsoOfNat` -- neither structural nor well-founded recursion over a decreasing Nat measure, and this kernel has no Set/Finset/Classical.choice. Ours (nat_prelude/nth.rs) is `Nat.nth (dec : Nat -> Bool) (bound n : Nat) : Nat`, a fuel-bounded search: an extra explicit `bound` argument replaces the classical finiteness split, and the predicate is Bool-decidable-by-construction rather than an arbitrary Prop. The TYPES differ (arity 3 vs 2, Bool vs Prop domain), so the mirror is a different proposition per the mirror-flip criterion's own 'different types' clause. Surface form carries a trailing space: `Nat.nth` is a literal substring of the unrelated, already-honest `Nat.nthRoot` family.

mathlib_source.note: the divergence is in the definition/recursion principle, not the pinned statement; not re-derivable by this gate

constructions.why: Mathlib's `def Nat.findGreatest (P : ℕ → Prop) [DecidablePred P] : ℕ → ℕ` elaborates the DecidablePred witness as an instance implicit, giving type `(ℕ → Prop) → ℕ → ℕ`. Ours (nat_prelude/find_greatest.rs) is the same structural recursion, but this kernel has no instance implicits, so the DecidablePred witness is an EXPLICIT argument -- type `Π (P : Nat → Prop), DecidablePred Nat P → Nat → Nat` -- and the branch is `Decidable.byCases` rather than `ite`. The definitional bodies agree extensionally but the TYPES differ, so every mirror stated against Mathlib's findGreatest is a different proposition.

mathlib_source.note: re-exported through Mathlib.Data.Nat.Find; the divergence is in the definition's type (explicit vs instance-implicit DecidablePred), not the pinned statement; not re-derivable by this gate

constructions.why: Mathlib's `def Nat.floorRoot (n a : ℕ) : ℕ := if n = 0 ∨ a = 0 then 0 else a.factorization.prod fun p k ↦ p ^ (k / n)` is a product over `a.factorization : Finsupp`. This kernel has no Finsupp/Finset, so that body cannot be written at all. Ours (nat_prelude/factorization_root.rs) is an extensionally-equal bounded downward Nat.rec search over candidate `b`, verified against Mathlib's closed form by simulation over 400 (n, a) pairs before any Rust was written. Same Nat.multichoose shape: a search standing in for a product Mathlib defines and this kernel cannot express.

mathlib_source.note: the divergence is in the definition's body (Finsupp product vs bounded search), not the pinned statement; not re-derivable by this gate

constructions.why: Mathlib's `def Nat.ceilRoot (n a : ℕ) : ℕ := if n = 0 ∨ a = 0 then 0 else a.factorization.prod fun p k ↦ p ^ ((k + n - 1) / n)` is a product over `a.factorization : Finsupp`, the divisibility-lattice adjoint of floorRoot. This kernel has no Finsupp/Finset. Ours (nat_prelude/factorization_root.rs) is an extensionally-equal bounded upward search with fuel `a`, verified against Mathlib's closed form by simulation over 400 (n, a) pairs before any Rust was written.

mathlib_source.note: the divergence is in the definition's body (Finsupp product vs bounded search), not the pinned statement; not re-derivable by this gate

constructions.why: Mathlib's `def Abundant (n : ℕ) : Prop := n < ∑ i ∈ properDivisors n, i` (FactorisationProperties.lean) is a Finset sum over `n.properDivisors`. This kernel has no Finset, so that body cannot be written at all. Ours (nat_prelude/abundant_deficient.rs, ADR-1100) is `Abundant n := Lt (mul 2 n) (sumDivisors n)`, where `sumDivisors` sums every divisor of `n` in `[0,n]` including `n` itself via `sumRange` -- provably equivalent to Mathlib's phrasing for n != 0 (sumDivisors n = properDivisorsSum + n) but a structurally different construction, not a Finset sum. The module doc reaches this conclusion itself, citing the `Nat.minFac`/`Nat.multichoose` mirror-flip criterion directly.

mathlib_source.note: the divergence is in the definition's body (Finset.sum over properDivisors vs a sumDivisors-based Lt), not the pinned statement; not re-derivable by this gate

constructions.why: Mathlib's `def Deficient (n : ℕ) : Prop := ∑ i ∈ properDivisors n, i < n` (FactorisationProperties.lean), the same Finset-sum shape as `Abundant`. Ours (nat_prelude/abundant_deficient.rs, ADR-1100) is `Deficient n := Lt (sumDivisors n) (mul 2 n)` -- provably equivalent for n != 0, structurally different, no Finset in this kernel to state Mathlib's version at all.

mathlib_source.note: the divergence is in the definition's body (Finset.sum over properDivisors vs a sumDivisors-based Lt), not the pinned statement; not re-derivable by this gate

constructions.why: Mathlib's `def Perfect (n : ℕ) : Prop := ∑ i ∈ properDivisors n, i = n ∧ 0 < n` (Divisors.lean) is a Finset sum with an explicit positivity conjunct. Ours (nat_prelude/perfect.rs) is `Perfect n := Eq (sumDivisors n) (mul 2 n)`, with no positivity conjunct at all -- and the two are not merely differently-constructed but EXTENSIONALLY different at n = 0: sumDivisors 0 = 0 = mul 2 0, so ours has `Perfect 0` TRUE, while Mathlib's `Perfect 0` is FALSE (`0 < 0` fails). Same Finset-sum-vs-sumDivisors divergence as `Nat.Abundant`/`Nat.Deficient` above, one step stronger.

mathlib_source.note: the divergence is in the definition's body (Finset.sum over properDivisors plus a positivity conjunct vs a bare sumDivisors equation), not the pinned statement; not re-derivable by this gate
